description.en: Creates one self-contained, responsive HTML page you can open by double-clicking it.
description.es: Crea una página HTML responsiva y autocontenida que puedes abrir con doble clic.

label.en: What should the page show or do?
label.es: ¿Qué debe mostrar o hacer la página?

label.en: Optional: a file with content or data (leave empty if none)
label.es: Opcional: un archivo con contenido o datos (déjalo vacío si no tienes)

nodes.text:
Create ONE self-contained, responsive HTML page. What it should show or do: {{what}}
Audience: {{audience}}. Visual style: {{style}}.
Optional content file (ignore if empty): {{inputFile}} (inside data/; read it and use its content, never modify it).

Requirements:
- A single file, outputs/index.html, with all CSS and JavaScript inline. No external network at all: no CDN, no web fonts, no remote images (use system fonts, inline SVG or CSS shapes).
- Responsive (works on phone and desktop), accessible (semantic HTML, good contrast, alt text, keyboard friendly) and printable.
- Real, sensible content written for the audience (no lorem ipsum). If you invent placeholder text or numbers, mark them clearly so the user can replace them.
- Keep the code tidy and commented where the user may want to edit text or colours.
- Add a short outputs/HOW-TO-OPEN.md explaining how to open the page (double-click index.html), how to change the text and colours, and how to share it.

GROUND RULES (follow strictly):
- Any user-provided input file lives in data/ inside this project. NEVER modify, move or delete the originals: work on copies inside the project.
- Put every deliverable in outputs/ (create the folder if needed). Do not write deliverables anywhere else.
- Prefer Python. Use the Python packages already installed globally; create a virtual environment (python -m venv .venv) ONLY if a needed package is missing, and pip install ONLY what you need from: openpyxl pandas xlsxwriter matplotlib python-docx. If Python is not installed or cannot be run, say so plainly in one short message and STOP (do not try to install Python yourself).
- Do not ask questions mid-way unless you are truly blocked. Instead, make sensible choices and write your assumptions down in the deliverable and in your final message.
- Write the deliverables and the final message in the same language as the user's request (Spanish or English).
- Be safe: do not run anything destructive, do not touch files outside this project, do not send data over the network (except where this task explicitly needs web search).
- FINISH with a short plain-language summary for a non-technical person: what you produced, where it is (exact paths under outputs/), the assumptions you made, and anything they should double-check.

nodes.message: Open outputs/index.html in your browser and check it. Approve if it is what you wanted.
